args.note: I've written cold-read.md. I'd put the book down at I01 p11, I02 p25 and I03 p43, and I'd buy the next issue for I01 and I02 but not I03. Issue 01, page 11 is where the whole class goes: the Measure, Seal and Covenant are dropped with no explanation, and pages 49–51 depend on them. The best stretches: the debt-on-his-birthday opening (p2), "It's sweating" (p16), the scrap sleeve (p29), Ada and her mother (pp38–40) and the dad's death (p48). The main problems: Alpha and the Covenant aren't explained until p40–42; Lock never speaks; the four Halyard scientists blur together; the Maker's Seal and the bands seem to be in two places (p11 vs p35/p44); Bi11bot's timeline doesn't fit p48; Mara/Mera, Lina/Leona and Ren/Renn get mixed up; every character talks in the same neat sayings, which teen readers will call AI-written; and the final "FINAL HUMAN QUESTION" reads like a worksheet.

args.note: Cold read B complete: all three issues read cold with page-level reactions, verdicts (put down: 11 / 25 / 52; next issue: yes / yes / no), and the whole-book close — page 11 loses the class, the dialogue's uniform proverb-register reads machine-made to a skeptical teen reader, and unresolved threads (the flood Mera ordered, Bi11bot's impossible relocation, the Seal/band continuity) are flagged as reader-visible holes.
